title: Dedupe the Batch Against History
subtitle: Flag the already-paid invoice before it can pay again
scenario: It is 11:00 AM. Before matching, run the batch against payment history. For each invoice, decide whether its identity key already appears in the paid records - and flag the one repeat so it can be held. A duplicate always wins over a clean match.
instructions: For each invoice, check whether its identity key appears in payment history.
Set foundInHistory to true only for the invoice that matches a paid record.
Set isDuplicate to the same value - a match in history means a duplicate.
Only INV-58962 should be flagged; the rest are clear.
Return a JSON array of the five rows, then validate.

intro.heading: Before you match: catch the repeat first

sections.title: Dedupe runs before matching
sections.body: There is no point matching an invoice that was already paid. The duplicate check is the first gate: it compares each invoice's identity to the paid history and pulls any repeat out of the flow.

sections.title: Match on the full identity key
sections.body: A repeat is vendor id + invoice number + invoice total, together. INV-58962 in today's batch matches a day-0 paid record on all three, so it is a duplicate. The other four do not appear in history at all.

sections.title: A duplicate always wins
sections.body: Even if a duplicate's price and receipt were perfect, it must not pay again. Flagging isDuplicate here guarantees the match decision routes it to an exception no matter what else is true about it.

takeaway.heading: Duplicate check complete
points: You ran the whole batch against payment history before any matching.
INV-58962 matched a day-0 paid record on the full identity key, so it is flagged as a duplicate.
The other four invoices are not in history and are clear to move to the match.
Flagging isDuplicate guarantees the repeat is routed to an exception - a duplicate always wins.
The workflow can now stop an already-paid invoice before it reaches the payment run.
